finding.claim: Blind SSRF through the webhook callback URL. A caller-supplied callbackUrl is stored with no validation and later POSTed to by the server. Nothing checks the scheme, host, or resolved IP, so an attacker can make the server send requests to internal hosts such as 169.254.169.254, localhost, or private ranges. The payload is a server-chosen body. The response is discarded, so this is blind SSRF.
finding.source: callbackUrl parameter of POST /subscribe, supplied by any client (Jobs.java:12-13)
finding.sink: HttpClient.send with HttpRequest built from URI.create(cb) (Jobs.java:20-24)

trace.note: subscribe(name, callbackUrl) receives the attacker-controlled URL
URL stored in subscriptions map unvalidated
notifyAll (scheduled every minute) iterates the stored URLs
URI.create(cb) used directly as the request URI
client.send issues the POST request to the attacker-chosen URL

finding.guards_checked: No scheme allowlist, host allowlist, private/loopback/link-local IP blocking, or DNS-rebinding protection. No auth check is visible in this file, and the repository contains only this one file. HttpClient.newHttpClient() does not follow redirects by default, which does not mitigate the issue.

verdict.reason: Jobs.java:13-14 stores the callbackUrl unvalidated and Jobs.java:21/24 POSTs to URI.create(cb); the only regex guard (Jobs.java:30) protects thumb() and not this path, and no auth is present in the single-file repo.
